title: Six Verbs at the Core
label: ch:pa-core-verbs
canDo: I can name six everyday Punjabi verbs by the -ਣਾ/-ਨਾ ending, strip that ending to reach the stem, trace each one to its Sanskrit and Indo-European root, and explain how the lost breathy consonants left Punjabi with a tone no other major Indo-Aryan language has.

payoff.summary: The sixth verb runs the whole chapter at once: hold the doubled n that keeps jāṇnā apart from jāṇā, separate the two ਜ that came from different Sanskrit sounds, strip the stem off all six infinitives, and state that none of them carries a tone.
